It appears exclusively in prophetic judgment oracles and always alongside shammah ('desolation'), forming a fixed pair that intensifies the picture of utter devastation. Jeremiah uses this word-pair repeatedly to describe the fate of Judah and the nations (Jer 19:8; 25:9, 18; 29:18; 51:37), while Micah 6:16 applies it to Samaria's legacy. Spanish 'silbido/burla' captures both the sound and the mockery, while Arabic cognate evidence points to the same hissing gesture."

Jeremiah deploys it against Jerusalem (Jer 19:8), the nations (Jer 25:9, 18), Babylon (Jer 51:37), and the exile...
